Class WhoService

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.core.service.WhoService
public class WhoService extends Object
Core service that resolves a Credential to a WhoPrincipal.

Resolution pipeline:

  1. Look up the credential UUID in CredentialIdentityRepository.
  2. Return empty if not linked.
  3. Load the identity from IdentityRepository.
  4. Return empty if not found or status is not IdentityStatus.ACTIVE.
  5. Resolve permissions via the registered PermissionsResolver.
  6. Return a populated WhoPrincipal.

It also deletes identities together with their credentials (deleteIdentity(UUID)) and purges credentials that are linked to no identity (purgeOrphanedCredentials()), through the CredentialRemovers it is given. Wiring is done by the autoconfigure module.

who-core needs no Spring at runtime. The @Transactional methods run in a transaction when Spring's transaction support is present, as it always is with who's starter.

    • deactivate

      @Transactional public boolean deactivate(UUID identityId)
      Deactivates an identity: sets it IdentityStatus.DISABLED. It keeps its credentials, roles and history, but no credential resolves to it (resolve(Credential)), so its next request is unauthenticated, and its sign-in links and passkeys are refused, until it is reactivated. Deactivating an inactive identity changes nothing.
      Parameters:
      identityId - the identity to deactivate
      Returns:
      true if the identity exists, false if there is no such identity

    • reactivate

      @Transactional public boolean reactivate(UUID identityId)
      Reactivates an identity: sets it IdentityStatus.ACTIVE, so its credentials resolve to it again. Reactivating an active identity changes nothing.
      Parameters:
      identityId - the identity to reactivate
      Returns:
      true if the identity exists, false if there is no such identity

    • deleteIdentity

      @Transactional public boolean deleteIdentity(UUID identityId)
      Deletes an identity together with its credentials. Each credential linked to the identity is offered to the credential removers until one deletes it, then unlinked. Deleting the identity then removes, by cascade, its role assignments, enrollment tokens and passkeys.

      Prefer this to deleting the who_identity row directly: credential rows do not reference the identity, so a direct delete leaves them behind (see purgeOrphanedCredentials()).

      Parameters:
      identityId - the identity to delete
      Returns:
      true if the identity was deleted, false if there is no such identity

    • purgeOrphanedCredentials

      @Transactional public int purgeOrphanedCredentials()
      Deletes every credential that is linked to no identity, such as those left behind when an identity row was deleted directly instead of through deleteIdentity(UUID).

      A credential saved for enrollment but not yet enrolled is linked to no identity either, so it is deleted too, as is a credential being registered between its save and its link. Run this when no enrollment or registration is in flight.

      Returns:
      the number of credentials deleted
